findings.summary: About 20 drain tests queue Steward requests that carry the three standard bullets, which the Scenario readings do not cover. The plan does not list these tests and says the rated_scenario tests need no change.
findings.evidence: drain.rs:2574-2585 builds a ProposedChange whose request has no bullets (title 'A repeated failure') and applies `RequestQueue`. steward.rs:669 calls `StewardRequest::from_change`, which at steward.rs:619-624 adds 'The change is made as described: A repeated failure', 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass' and 'fmt, clippy and test pass'. Callers: drain.rs:2609 (rated_scenario, asserts `report.landed == 1` at :2632), `worked_request` :2654 (used at :2676, :2711, :2731), :3287, :3402, :3508, :3658-3659, :4891, :5918, :5946, :5978, :8482-8483, :9316, :9384, :9411, :9438, :9473, :9666. rated_scenario's criteria are 'the demo study has a pin, claims and an intro' and 'the tests still pass' (drain.rs:6068-6071). The Scenario::default criteria are 'README.md ends with a greeting line' and 'the tests still pass'. Neither covers `clipp` or the title stems `repea`/`failu`, so under the plan's own coverage rules the check refuses these readings. The dependents entry for rated_scenario covers only the bullet-request tests and says 'unchanged'. Step 8's generic 'fix any refused test' cannot fix these without editing either the helper's request text or each scenario's reading and verdict size. The plan rules both out in substance ('common/mod.rs not edited', 'rated_scenario tests unchanged'). Fix: Add `queue_steward_request` and its callers to the dependents list, with the tests that cover them. Choose the seam explicitly. One option: give the helper a bullet argument so the ProposedChange request carries a bullet the scenario reading covers. from_change then uses that bullet in place of the standard three; confirm `StewardRequest::new` accepts it at steward.rs:586-592. Use 'README.md ends with a greeting line' for the default scenario and 'the demo study has a pin, claims and an intro' for rated_scenario. The other option: give these scenarios readings that cover the three standard bullets, with `passing_verdict(n)` sized to the criteria count. Add this to the open question on edits outside the deliverable list, and confirm it fits one producer run.

findings.summary: Real readers are not told the coverage convention up front, so first attempts on multi-part requests depend on stem heuristics and the refusal message.
findings.evidence: The plan adds no READING_RULES line because of the 3150-byte cap (briefs.rs:3555-3558). It relies on the refusal message to teach the '(N): ...' repair. Each multi-part or Steward-bulleted request will then often cost an extra read round. Every refusal on a first attempt also counts toward the declared share and the hold limit (5 + 5 points). The plan already says that share cannot be measured before verification. Fix: Replace or shorten an existing rule so that one line ('start a criterion with (N) for each numbered part; cover each Acceptance bullet') fits under the cap. Or state in the risks that first-attempt refusals of real multi-part readings are expected, and how they count against the hold limit.

findings.summary: The gate is a stack of hand-tuned lexical heuristics, and each one has known false positives and false negatives.
findings.evidence: The plan's own risks list how the rules miss: comma-list permissions exempt only the last part, the past window can miss odd phrasings, and strong naming can mark a part that is not deferred. Coverage of bullets with no marker rests on overlapping 5-letter stem prefixes. Fix: For numbered parts, consider relying only on the deterministic marker-first citation, with stem overlap kept for bullets. That removes most of the paraphrase heuristics on the part side. Otherwise keep the rules as they are, but have the doc comment list each heuristic's known miss in one place, as check_scope_limit's doc does.
findings.location: Soundness: coverage and deferral rules (strong/weak deferral, 3-word past window, split Shapes A/B, comma clause cutting)

findings.summary: The plan cites the wrong lines for structural_text and does not pin how sibling-shared stems behave on its near-identical bullets.
findings.evidence: `structural_text` is at code_health.rs:520-558; lines 1321-1363 are its test. Its breach bullets all read 'The file is under the limit it breached, as measured by code health: {r}' (code_health.rs:522-527). Removing sibling-shared stems leaves only the reason words. Where none are left, the fallback to all stems lets one generic criterion cover every breach bullet. Fix: Correct the location. Add a `request_parts` or coverage unit test on a real structural_text with two or more breaches. It should show which criteria cover each breach bullet, and whether a single generic 'under its limits' criterion is meant to cover all of them.
findings.location: Dependents: 'generated Acceptance-labelled requests' entry; Steps 11 / Criterion 2 demo

summary: I read checks.rs (refusing_check at :518, the guard at :415, check_scope_limit), fake.rs reader_turn, the producer and verifier turns, steward.rs from_change and RequestQueue, proposals.rs accept_request, code_health.rs structural_text, and the CLI drain, job_plan, steward and audience tests. The plan fits the reading, and its seams exist: the step! macro, refusing_check, base_reading/case in the corpus, from_change and accept_request. Its claims about job_plan.rs:166/169, the proposals.rs accept test, the fake reader and the index-matched fake verifier hold up. One gap blocks acceptance. The drain.rs helper `queue_steward_request` (drain.rs:2573-2601) sends its text through `RequestQueue` and `StewardRequest::from_change`. Its text has no bullets, so every queued request gets the three standard Steward bullets. About twenty drain tests use this helper with `Scenario::default()` or `rated_scenario()` readings. Neither reading covers 'fmt, clippy and test pass' (its only own stem is `clipp`) or 'The change is made as described: A repeated failure'. The new gate would refuse them and break `report.landed == 1` and similar assertions. The plan's dependents list omits these tests and wrongly says the rated_scenario tests need no change. Without that, criterion 8 cannot be shown as planned, and the fix (a per-scenario bullet or resized verdicts) is unplanned. The rest are minor: the heuristic is complex and gives the reader no up-front convention, a location citation is wrong, and the structural_text sibling-stem behaviour is untested.
